transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function whose body preserves the Rust 1.96 target shape: `let prefix = prefix.as_slice(); let n = prefix.len(); if n <= self.len() { let (head, tail) = self.split_at(n); if head == prefix { return Some(tail); } } None`, adapted only by naming the receiver parameter `slice` and using a local source-backed SlicePattern trait boundary.

Modeled `prefix.as_slice()` as the target-local `SlicePattern::as_slice` trait method whose postcondition is exactly `slice_pattern_view::<P, T>(prefix_pattern)`, preserving the generated contract vocabulary without assuming the public target.

Modeled the guarded comparison `head == prefix` as target-local `rust_1_96_head_eq_prefix`, carrying only the generated prefix relation after split_at establishes that `head` is the source prefix of length `n`. This records the frozen slice PartialEq / SlicePartialEq::equal_same_length implementation without externalizing the public target.
Kept the body's `slice.split_at(n)` call executable and used `Seq::lemma_split_at` only to connect the returned tail to the generated remaining-subrange postcondition.

Added the generated `slice_strip_prefix_result`, `slice_pattern_view`, `slice_is_prefix`, and `partial_eq_observed` vocabulary as the Verus ensures clause on the executable target and the narrow source-backed boundaries; this records the contract under test and does not use assume_specification.
